title: Issue 1 Cover — Mandatory Proximity
summary: RELEASED COVER CANON. Preserve the existing approved Stardust Station Issue 1 cover rather than redesigning it. Its selling job is ensemble introduction: an inviting, crowded orbital workplace full of distinct coworkers, with the enormous two-line STARDUST STATION masthead establishing the line's commercial identity. If regeneration is ever required, the exact pixel reference is the visual authority for composition, trade dress and rendered character arrangement; do not reinterpret it from text alone.
settingText: Released Issue 1 cover composition: bright polished Stardust Station workplace with a starfield/planet glimpse at the left edge, clean StarTrust architecture, foreground workstation surfaces and the established ensemble arranged below the masthead.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED COVER IMAGE. Reproduce the released Issue 1 cover composition from the approved pixel reference rather than designing a new alternative. The existing cover is canon.

TRADE DRESS AUTHORITY. Pixel-read production/references/stardust-station/issue-01-cover-trade-dress.jpg. Preserve the large two-line white STARDUST STATION masthead with dark blue shadow/outline and cyan orbital swoosh/star accents; Star Splitter Visions publisher bug at upper left; ISSUE #1 at upper right; MANDATORY PROXIMITY centered beneath the masthead.

THUMBNAIL READ. The masthead must dominate first, then the central smiling human woman and surrounding visibly different coworkers. Preserve the bright blue-violet station field and strong character silhouettes that make the released cover readable when small.

Do not modernize, simplify, restage, recolor, substitute characters, convert the cover into a collage, or add new text. This recipe exists to make the released cover available as cover-production authority, not to reopen the design.

title: Issue 2 Cover
summary: Sell Issue 2 through one concrete workplace absurdity: the future has mastered orbital life but the shared break room has become a tiny bureaucracy. A normal lunch should feel like it requires procedural clearance. The cover promises character comedy and escalating governance without revealing how the crew resolves any rule or policy.
settingText: Stardust Station shared break room: maintained microwave, shared refrigerator, vending unit, mismatched chairs and practical counter space, now crowded by excessive blank notices, arrows, forms and procedural clutter. Bright ordinary StarTrust workplace, not dystopian.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED COVER IMAGE. One dominant gag, not a montage: Jax stands at the microwave holding an ordinary lunch container while a ridiculous but neatly organized thicket of blank policy cards, arrows and forms surrounds the appliance. Astra is just behind him with one fresh form; Brick looms at the edge treating the situation with unnecessary seriousness.

FOCAL HIERARCHY. First read: the giant STARDUST STATION masthead. Second: Jax plus the microwave/lunch. Third: the absurd procedural clutter. Astra and Brick support the joke but must not compete with the lunch-vs-bureaucracy image.

COMPOSITION. Keep the top quarter visually quiet enough for the established masthead system. Use a slightly low, close workplace angle so the microwave and paperwork create a strong central shape. Avoid a flat three-character lineup.
THUMBNAIL READ. At small size the image must still read as ONE PERSON + ONE LUNCH + TOO MANY RULES. Do not depend on tiny signs or legible prop text for the joke.
SPOILER CEILING. Do not depict the final break-room rules, a solved governance system, a triumphant meal, or any end-of-issue consensus. The cover sells the problem, not the fix.

directionInline.text: Exact required cover text: STARDUST STATION / ISSUE #2. Render only this required cover lettering plus the established Star Splitter Visions publisher bug from the trade-dress reference. Do not invent taglines, blurbs, credits, character labels or promotional copy.

Use the Issue 1 cover pixel reference for trade dress only; use released Issue 1 interiors and the active Stardust visual-reference pack for character and break-room appearance. Do not invent an Issue 2 subtitle: current production data supplies none.
Tone: bright, polished, warm workplace comedy. The bureaucracy is ridiculous, not sinister. No grimdark, no malfunction crisis, no environmental text that the reader must decipher.

title: Issue 3 Cover
summary: Sell Issue 3 as a social ownership problem made physically irresistible: three completely ordinary tasks need names in the OWNER field, and nobody wants to become the person nearest the pen. The cover should make harmless folders feel more dangerous than a cosmic anomaly without revealing who ultimately owns anything.
settingText: Small operations meeting table in the Stardust Station admin hub with three task folders/work cards, pens, tablets, drinks and more chairs than the meeting deserves; ordinary station work remains visible beyond.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED COVER IMAGE. Place three plain task folders/cards huge in the near foreground, each with a conspicuously EMPTY owner line represented graphically but without requiring readable environmental wording. A pen lies between them like a social hazard.

SOCIAL GEOMETRY. Astra sits or stands at the far side of the table trying to hold the meeting together. Jax, Zib and Glorp occupy clearly different positions but all subtly lean, turn or reach AWAY from the folders. Empty chairs imply the rest of the crew rather than crowding nine faces onto the cover.
FOCAL HIERARCHY. Masthead first; three ownerless tasks second; coworkers' evasive body language third. The joke should survive even if facial expressions are unreadable at thumbnail size.

COMPOSITION. Use converging table lines to point directly at the three folders. Keep the upper trade-dress zone clean and maintain bright clean station color rather than turning the meeting room into drab office beige.
SPOILER CEILING. Do not reveal the eventual task assignments, who volunteers, who is pressured, or the meeting's resolution. No completed owner names.

directionInline.text: Exact required cover text: STARDUST STATION / ISSUE #3. Render only this required cover lettering plus the established Star Splitter Visions publisher bug from the trade-dress reference. Do not invent taglines, blurbs, credits, character labels or promotional copy.

Use the Issue 1 cover pixel reference for masthead, publisher bug, issue-number behavior and overall cover-brand continuity only. Interior released art controls the coworkers' appearance. Do not invent an Issue 3 subtitle: current production data supplies none.
The cover is a character-comedy poster built from posture and distance, not a recap collage or generic meeting scene.

title: Issue 4 Cover — Temporary Material
summary: Sell the irresistible practical dilemma at the heart of Temporary Material: the correct replacement part is far away, the fault is here now, and one small piece of unusual residue might be useful if the crew refuses to pretend it is more than it is. Competence under constraint is the hook; the strange material must remain physically ordinary and scientifically unresolved.
settingText: Bright maintained Stardust Station maintenance bay with one open wall service panel, a visibly absent bracket/component position, approved clamps and mesh on the work cart, and one small non-glowing fragment/sample of odd residue in a tray.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED COVER IMAGE. Zib owns the foreground: one approved clamp in hand, looking from the open service panel to the small residue fragment on the workbench. Astra watches the practical choice; Mira is interested in the material but not treating it as a miracle.

COVER HOOK. Make the missing proper part visually obvious through the open bracket location / empty parts tray. The strange residue is physically small. The image should ask: would you use THAT to keep THIS running?
FOCAL HIERARCHY. Masthead; Zib + clamp + missing part; tiny residue sample; Astra/Mira reactions. Never let the residue become the largest or brightest object.
PALETTE AND LIGHT. Clean industrial cyan/teal with restrained amber work lights and ordinary metallic hardware. No mystical glow, sacred framing, cosmic particles or fantasy-material spectacle.
THUMBNAIL READ. A mechanic, an open machine, a missing piece, and one questionable substitute. The central dilemma must survive without text.
SPOILER CEILING. Do not show the final temporary brace, successful live cycles, the report, commercial-interest flag, or the later corporate consequence.

directionInline.text: Exact required cover text: STARDUST STATION / TEMPORARY MATERIAL / ISSUE #4. Render only this required cover lettering plus the established Star Splitter Visions publisher bug from the trade-dress reference. Do not invent taglines, blurbs, credits, character labels or promotional copy.

Pixel-read the released Issue 1 cover for trade dress. Use released/current Stardust references for Zib, Astra, Mira and maintenance-bay design. Preserve the issue title exactly as TEMPORARY MATERIAL.
This cover sells practical uncertainty, not discovery. Do not make the residue look powerful, sentient, valuable or understood.

title: Issue 5 Cover — Resource Efficiency Review
summary: Sell the temptation, not merely the bureaucracy: StarTrust's shiny resource-efficiency pilot is intruding into ordinary work, and participating may help Stardust reach a desperately needed replacement part faster. The cover should make corporate nonsense materially attractive enough to create a real choice.
settingText: Main Bullpen / Admin Hub being physically colonized by pristine StarTrust collection bins, sample containers, neat review hardware and polished corporate packets while normal tools, work orders and maintenance carts still need the same floor space.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED COVER IMAGE. Astra stands at the visual fork between two concrete things: a conspicuously empty replacement-part tray / unresolved maintenance component to one side and a pristine corporate collection container/pilot kit arriving from the other. She is not villainously tempted; she is doing the math.

Jax works around the corporate container rather than posing with it; Mira holds or examines a small legitimate sample at the edge. Their ordinary work should visibly continue while the program infrastructure expands.
FOCAL HIERARCHY. Masthead; Astra between NEED and PROGRAM; the physical pilot hardware; Jax/Mira as evidence that the question affects real work. Do not clutter the cover with every form or subplot.

VISUAL CONTRAST. Corporate hardware is clean, pristine and slightly too coordinated. Stardust work gear is equally maintained but practical and lived-in. Neither side is dark or evil; the tension is incentive.
THUMBNAIL READ. One woman between an empty needed-part space and a shiny new corporate apparatus. The choice must be legible before any details.
SPOILER CEILING. Do not show the crew's final boundary, the exact accepted/refused pilot terms, successful sample collection, Wellness Baseline Week, or later procurement result.

directionInline.text: Exact required cover text: STARDUST STATION / RESOURCE EFFICIENCY REVIEW / ISSUE #5. Render only this required cover lettering plus the established Star Splitter Visions publisher bug from the trade-dress reference. Do not invent taglines, blurbs, credits, character labels or promotional copy.
Use the Issue 1 cover only for trade dress; use released/current production references for character identity and the admin hub. Preserve RESOURCE EFFICIENCY REVIEW exactly.
Do not turn Corporate into a sinister visual faction. The cover works only if the offer looks reasonable enough to be dangerous.

title: Issue 6 Cover — Wellness Week
summary: Sell Wellness Week through one perfect physical contradiction: an aggressively serene mandatory wellness setup is blocking the service access Zib needs for a ten-minute repair. The cover should communicate the whole issue before the reader can finish reading the subtitle.
settingText: Multipurpose room converted into bright corporate wellness space: carefully arranged chairs, water, soft lights and cheerful blank materials placed directly in front of an ordinary wall service panel that maintenance needs to open.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED COVER IMAGE. The center of the image is an immaculate row or semicircle of wellness chairs. Directly behind them, half-obscured, is the service panel. Zib stands with a compact tool case looking at the chairs, then the inaccessible panel.

Astra is caught between program setup and maintenance access, visibly realizing this is now her problem. Noola may occupy or approach one chair, reinforcing that the room is physically real and warm rather than merely symbolic.
FOCAL HIERARCHY. Masthead; serene chairs blocking service panel; Zib with tools; Astra's recognition. The joke should not require a banner or readable wellness slogan.

PALETTE. Preserve Stardust's blue-violet station identity but let the wellness materials introduce slightly softer teal/violet/white accents. Avoid beige spa imagery and generic mindfulness iconography.
THUMBNAIL READ. Chairs in the way of a mechanic. That is sufficient.
SPOILER CEILING. Do not show the repair completed, people walking out, the room being cleared, the quiet-room solution, collected data, or the program's eventual outcome.

directionInline.text: Exact required cover text: STARDUST STATION / WELLNESS WEEK / ISSUE #6. Render only this required cover lettering plus the established Star Splitter Visions publisher bug from the trade-dress reference. Do not invent taglines, blurbs, credits, character labels or promotional copy.
Pixel-read Issue 1 cover trade dress and preserve established Zib/Astra/Noola identity from proper references. Preserve WELLNESS WEEK exactly.
The humor is spatial and practical. No villainous corporate imagery, no meditation parody faces, no fake catastrophe.

title: Issue 7 Cover — Bring Your Feelings to Work Day
summary: Sell the issue through the dangerous ambiguity of an anonymous feelings program inside a real workplace. A single disclosure system may contain a maintenance problem, a process problem, a private human truth or an absurd grievance; the cover should promise that the crew will have to distinguish them without revealing which card becomes which outcome.
settingText: Main Bullpen / Admin Hub with a cheerful temporary participation table: anonymous cards, privacy envelopes, pens and a drop box inserted into ordinary work traffic; the vending machine is visible deeper in the environment.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED COVER IMAGE. A bright anonymous-disclosure box/card station dominates the foreground. Kreeb is the calm privacy guardian beside it. Noola holds a sealed or folded card without revealing its content. Brick, farther back, suspiciously studies the vending machine as if it has become a legitimate case.
Do not draw literal branching labels or spoiler categories. Instead, use environmental staging to suggest that identical-looking cards can point toward radically different realities.

FOCAL HIERARCHY. Masthead; anonymous card/drop box; Noola's private card; Brick-versus-vending-machine secondary joke. Kreeb anchors the tone so the cover never mocks the existence of genuine feeling.
PALETTE. Cheerful corporate card colors can puncture the normal blue/cyan station palette, but keep the overall cover polished and coherent rather than rainbow-cluttered.
THUMBNAIL READ. One anonymous box, one private card, one ridiculous suspicious glance. The reader should immediately wonder what is in the box.
SPOILER CEILING. Do not reveal Noola's actual disclosure text, the cold-condition hatch fault, the duplicate-process discovery, the ultimate reporting boundary, or the corporate-visit consequence.

directionInline.text: Exact required cover text: STARDUST STATION / BRING YOUR FEELINGS TO WORK DAY / ISSUE #7. Render only this required cover lettering plus the established Star Splitter Visions publisher bug from the trade-dress reference. Do not invent taglines, blurbs, credits, character labels or promotional copy.
Use Issue 1 cover pixels for trade dress and proper released/current references for Kreeb, Noola, Brick and the station. Preserve BRING YOUR FEELINGS TO WORK DAY exactly.
The cover must respect real emotion while preserving dry workplace comedy. Brick's vending-machine suspicion is a secondary counterpoint, not the thesis.

title: Issue 8 Cover — The Corporate Visit
summary: Sell observation itself as pressure. One competent StarTrust Operations Liaison arrives without an entourage, and the crew has been told to operate normally. The visitor is not a villain; the irresistible question is what 'normal' looks like when someone with institutional authority is actually watching.
settingText: Stardust Station docking vestibule opening onto the bright working level. Clean hatch, temporary visitor badge point, route markings and normal work visible beyond. One compact professional case; no ceremonial reception.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED COVER IMAGE. Frame the open docking hatch as a strong geometric threshold. The Operations Liaison steps through with one compact case, calm and observant. Astra receives them several meters inside the station while Jax is already checking or clearing the actual route.

The station behind them must remain active: carts, workstations, service activity and coworkers continuing their shift rather than forming a reception line. This is a workplace being seen, not a delegation arriving at a palace.
FOCAL HIERARCHY. Masthead; Liaison in the hatch; Astra/Jax and the lived-in station beyond. The visitor should feel consequential because of framing and attention, not because of menace.
LIGHT. Use bright docking white/cyan at the threshold and richer blue-violet station depth beyond. Keep the liaison visually distinct but within StarTrust design language.
THUMBNAIL READ. One person entering, a whole workplace visible behind them. The doorway itself is the tension.
SPOILER CEILING. Do not show the galley fault, live repair, residue sample, visitor conclusion, limited-pilot recommendation, central target, or any outcome of the visit.

directionInline.text: Exact required cover text: STARDUST STATION / THE CORPORATE VISIT / ISSUE #8. Render only this required cover lettering plus the established Star Splitter Visions publisher bug from the trade-dress reference. Do not invent taglines, blurbs, credits, character labels or promotional copy.
Pixel-read the Issue 1 cover for trade dress. Use the current character shelf and visual reference pack for Astra, Jax and the Operations Liaison. Preserve THE CORPORATE VISIT exactly.
Do not portray the Liaison as sinister, smug or hostile. Competence and reasonable institutional pressure are more interesting.

title: Issue 9 Cover — Output Target
summary: Sell the metric's seductive authority. A large pristine progress target has no ability to repair machinery, unload cargo or judge whether work needs doing, yet it has become the most visually important object in the room. Astra must look between the number and the station she actually manages.
settingText: Main Bullpen / Admin Hub with one enormous clean abstract target/progress-ring display dominating the upper middle field while maintenance tools, route sheets, cargo equipment and real work continue underneath it.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED COVER IMAGE. Astra is the human focal point below a huge abstract corporate target/progress graphic. She looks from the target toward actual work happening on two sides: Zib with maintenance hardware and Jax moving real cargo/route material.
The target must be visually clean, seductive and authoritative—not evil, glitching or red-alert-like. It should be the kind of graphic people naturally want to improve.
FOCAL HIERARCHY. Masthead; giant target; Astra caught between number and work; Zib/Jax demonstrating what the number cannot understand.

COMPOSITION. Let the circular target echo the orbital swoosh language of the masthead without merging into it. Keep the top trade-dress zone legible and use strong diagonals from real work toward Astra.
THUMBNAIL READ. One enormous target over one manager and two lanes of real work. Avoid tiny dashboards and unreadable charts.
SPOILER CEILING. Do not show the cargo-delay consequence, target progress values, Astra stopping the schedule, missed benchmark, final report, or the decision to reject output scheduling.

directionInline.text: Exact required cover text: STARDUST STATION / OUTPUT TARGET / ISSUE #9. Render only this required cover lettering plus the established Star Splitter Visions publisher bug from the trade-dress reference. Do not invent taglines, blurbs, credits, character labels or promotional copy.
Use Issue 1 pixels for trade dress and proper visual references for Astra, Zib, Jax and station work areas. Preserve OUTPUT TARGET exactly.
No readable metric number is required. The target's visual authority should be understood without fake interface copy.

title: Issue 10 Cover — The Station Stays Open
summary: Sell the season finale as an act of definition before the outcome is known. Corporate has provided several polished institutional futures, none of which describe Stardust Station. The crew has four hours to create a fourth answer while ordinary work continues. The cover should feel decisive and hopeful without revealing whether the fourth option is accepted.
settingText: Main Bullpen / Admin Hub worktable under a deadline: several polished standardized corporate option cards/forms laid out side by side, one plain blank fourth sheet and pen beside them, ordinary work orders and maintenance gear continuing around the table, active station visible beyond.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED COVER IMAGE. Astra's hand is physically placing or pulling the plain fourth sheet beside the polished corporate options. Her face is visible and resolved but not triumphant. Mira, Zib and Jax are present only as partial coworkers / hands / working figures contributing tools, records or evidence around the table rather than posing.
The working station beyond the table remains visibly alive. This matters: the question is not whether the station deserves a heroic rescue, but how to describe what it already does.
FOCAL HIERARCHY. Masthead; blank fourth sheet against polished options; Astra's decisive hand/face; evidence of ordinary crew work. Do not turn the cover into an ensemble victory portrait.

COLOR AND MOOD. Preserve the confident blue-white Stardust palette with warmer practical work lights. The image can feel more open and spacious than earlier covers, signaling possibility without visually declaring victory.
THUMBNAIL READ. Several identical polished choices plus one plain fourth sheet. The fourth sheet must read instantly as the disruptive object.

SPOILER CEILING. Do not show the fourth option's final wording, central approval, procurement improvement, permanent repair arrival, celebration, or the issue's final status. The cover ends at the choice to define the station honestly.

directionInline.text: Exact required cover text: STARDUST STATION / THE STATION STAYS OPEN / ISSUE #10. Render only this required cover lettering plus the established Star Splitter Visions publisher bug from the trade-dress reference. Do not invent taglines, blurbs, credits, character labels or promotional copy.
Pixel-read the released Issue 1 cover for trade dress and use the proper visual references for Astra, Mira, Zib, Jax and the admin hub. Preserve THE STATION STAYS OPEN exactly.
Finale energy comes from agency and definition, not explosions or triumphant spectacle. The reader must still need to open the issue to learn whether the fourth option survives.
